A1.justification: Both PDFs describe THINK, with matching methods, equations, experiments, and shared appendices. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the complete documents, including v3's added Appendices E–G.

before.justification: v2 reports original LongBench and Needle-in-a-Haystack evaluations, memory measurements, pruning ablations, and cache analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds standalone pruning experiments, latency and throughput measurements, and SVD-method comparisons.

M1.justification: The query-driven channel scores, greedy selection, recent-token preservation, masking procedure, KIVI integration, and value-cache pruning equations remain unchanged. Expanded implementation explanations and experiments on vanilla models do not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same LongBench tasks, Needle-in-a-Haystack tests, and synthetic workload with input/output lengths of 160/338. The added experiments change compression configurations and measurements within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 12 adds an evaluated comparison family: Palu on Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 and ASVD on LLaMA-2-7B-Chat. Existing H2O, SnapKV, KIVI, and norm-based comparisons remain. Eigen Attention is newly cited but is not an evaluated baseline in that table.

E3.justification: v3 substantially extends evaluation beyond accuracy and memory: Appendix F introduces TTFT, TPOT, and throughput measurements, specifying batch size 300 for timing. Appendix E adds full-cache controls without companion compression. Appendix G introduces purportedly matched-compression comparisons, although its 'compressed by 80%' wording conflicts with the stated 20% total-cache reduction for THINK(0.4), leaving exact matching unclear.

E4.justification: Appendix E tests whether THINK remains effective without token eviction or quantization, varying channel pruning from 40% to 60% on two existing models. This adds a focused control and sensitivity analysis. Existing recent-size, equal-memory, retrieval-depth, and joint key/value analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The added tables continue reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Tables 1–8 and the existing figures retain their results; Tables 9–12 add substantial new outcomes. Table 9 reports LLaMA-3 standalone averages of 41.86 for vanilla and 42.27/42.25 at 40%/50% pruning. Table 10 reports KIVI TPOT of 0.27 versus 0.25/0.24 ms/token with THINK, alongside TTFT of 7.0 versus 10.4/10.2 ms. Table 11 adds throughput results, and Table 12 adds SVD-comparator scores.

T1.justification: The pruning optimization, channel-selection criteria, Equations 1–4, and Appendix A's SVD energy definition are unchanged. No new formal assumption, theorem, proof, or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The central contribution and channel-pruning claims remain. The abstract clarifies batch-size capacity as increasing from 4× with KIVI alone to 5× with THINK, while the conclusion now qualifies efficiency by acknowledging increased time to first token.

C2.justification: v3 explains the tradeoff between channel-importance computation increasing prefilling latency and reduced memory traffic improving decoding. Section 4.4 and Appendix D newly connect harder value-cache pruning to more uniform channel magnitudes. The conclusion explicitly identifies timing overhead and further value-cache pruning research as limitations.

D1.justification: v3 adds a THINK code-availability statement and repository address. Appendix F supplies batch size 300 for the new timing experiments. Existing A100 hardware disclosures, pooling and observation-window settings, and Appendix C's quantization implementation are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix G adds targeted positioning against Palu, ASVD, and Eigen Attention, contrasting direct online pruning with calibrated low-rank decomposition and cache reconstruction. Two Lu et al. papers are also newly cited. The established positioning against eviction, quantization, and structured pruning remains.

P1.justification: v3 makes targeted abstract, implementation, results-discussion, and conclusion edits. Section 6 becomes 'Conclusion and Limitations,' Appendix D expands, Appendices E–G are appended, and the header changes to ICLR 2025 publication status. The main narrative and section order remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 9–12 and adjusts appendix placement: Figures 4 and 5 share a page, Figure 6 moves to the following page, and Table 8 shares space with Table 9. All seven existing figure graphics and the structures of Tables 1–8 are retained.

improvement.justification: Standalone controls in Table 9 and measured latency/throughput tradeoffs in Tables 10–11 strengthen practical validation beyond v2's memory measurements. Explicit limitations and code-access information improve transparency. These gains are bounded: Appendix G's inconsistent compression wording weakens confidence in its claimed matched comparisons, while the central method and earlier evidence remain unchanged.
